transcript.text: Part Two. You will hear a hostess talking on a radio program to her audience about how to rent a bike.
First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 15.
Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 15.
Hello listeners, it's your host Sarah here again on the award-winning program How to.
Last week we looked intentionally on how to rent a car, and today we would be discussing how to rent a bike in the little town of Chuga.
As usual, we are not advertising for any company, but we just want to help our listeners know the best way to go about renting a bike.
We bring you the easiest and best methods of doing things, so let's go right in.
From wherever you are, you drive or walk to the bike station, you then put your finger on the screen of a bike.
Make sure you use your bare hand, gloves or clothes cannot be recognised, but don't touch the alarm on the side as it's quite sensitive.
Next, input the password number, which is unique each time and can be applied for all systems, and then you would see a button appear.
Once it appears, just click it and then undo the lock of the bike.
Please note that payment has to have been made prior to this or at least half payment by cash to the bike company.
Remember that the cashier would ask for your proof of payment before directing you to where the bikes are.
Once you get the bike, it is important you understand a few safety measures before setting out.
On this programme, we always emphasise the fact that life is important to us, and as a matter of fact, we still need you around here.
So, make sure you do not ride without your helmet.
Also, make sure that if you have a passenger, they have one too.
We have been receiving far too many reports of bike accidents that resulted in deaths from head injuries.
So please let us all adhere to these safety measures. They are for our own good.
After riding safely and returning, you can return the bike to the rack and make sure that it is well placed.
Then lock the bike, and you would know when it is properly locked by the light which would turn on.
Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 16 to 20.
Now listen and answer questions 16 to 20.
So, here we are at our improved bike renting centre.
The renovation is not yet complete, but I am sure you will agree that it looks a lot better than before.
We hope that the new layout and amenities will convince people to begin cycling again.
In the middle of the facility is the bicycle area.
Now, guests can select a bike rather than just being handed one by staff.
Another complaint before was that there was nowhere for customers to take a rest.
So, on the right side of the facility, just two doors down from the ATM is the coffee bar.
It's spacious enough to fit 20 people.
We also have a much bigger meeting room located by the fountain.
It is mostly for discussing bicycle races.
Situated next to the ATM is the maintenance office.
What's cool about it is that there are glass walls that allow guests to see the staff repair the bikes.
The locker room for guests is on the left side just before the exit.
In the past, guests had to leave their personal belongings in their car or with a friend, but now there's a locker available for all riders.
However, it is just to keep their things. The changing area is next door.
Don't worry, there is a divider to separate the men from the women.
As for the employees, there is a staff toilet next to the exit on the right side.
Aside from the usual toilet and think, there is even a shower for employees' depression.
That is the end of part two. You now have half a minute to check your answers to part two.
